comparisons.peer_summary: The Company has four reportable segments: Data Center (including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, etc.), Client (CPUs, APUs, chipsets for desktops/notebooks), Gaming (discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoCs), and Embedded (embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, SOMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD explicitly define their Data Center/AI networking segments as key components of their semiconductor business models. AVGO highlights its role in 'AI networking and connectivity' for data centers, while AMD defines its Data Center segment to include 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerators' and 'SmartNICs'. Both companies treat AI-enabled data center solutions as a primary growth driver within their segment reporting, although AVGO focuses on the networking connectivity aspect and AMD on the compute acceleration aspect.

comparisons.peer_summary: Business is organized into Intel Products, Intel Foundry, and All other; CCG, DCAI, and Intel Foundry are reportable operating segments, while NEX, Altera, and Mobileye are non-reportable segments with selective disclosure.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and Intel (INTC) disclose specific reportable segments focused on data center and AI workloads. AVGO's Semiconductor Solutions segment includes 'data center, service provider, and enterprise networking applications, including AI networking'. Similarly, Intel's reportable segments include the 'Data Center and AI (DCAI)' segment. While AVGO structures its business by product type (semiconductor solutions) which encompasses these applications, Intel structures by operating group, but both explicitly isolate AI and data center performance as key strategic and reporting dimensions.
